item.title: CAP Theory and Raft implementation in TiDB placement driver
item.description: The CAP theorem states what a replicated store can guarantee when the network splits. Raft implements CAP’s CP choice via majority quorum. This post introduces that theory (C, A, P, partition trade-off, Raft as CP), then details PD’s embedded-etcd Raft. TiKV Region Multi-Raft is in TiKV; PD TSO / locate / schedule surfaces are in TiDB architecture.

item.title: TiDB architecture: cluster topology, TiDB server and Placement Driver
item.description: TiDB is a MySQL-compatible distributed SQL system. A deployment is a cluster of TiDB servers (compute), PD (control), TiKV (row store), and optionally TiFlash (columnar). This post orients cluster roles, follows one TiDB server in git/tidb (dispatch → execute), then shows how PD in git/pd owns Region key ranges (split/merge), TSO, locate, and scheduling. TiKV store, Region Raft, and 2PC are in TiKV; CAP theory and PD etcd Raft are in CAP and Raft.
